inputProfiles.owner-source: The owning package sources, tests and its workspace dependency closure, plus shared execution configuration and runtime identity.
inputProfiles.workspace-records: owner-source plus the authored .ia record tree, schemas, guides and native fixture inventories these tasks read through filesystem discovery.
inputProfiles.installed-cli: workspace-records plus every app, package and distribution source and the native generators, because the task runs the built CLI through its path, which no import edge names, so its own hash must cover what the CLI is built from.
inputProfiles.tooling: The tools tree, root TypeScript and Vitest configuration, and the repository manifests and lockfile.
inputProfiles.repository-inventory: Every tracked and nonignored file, because these checks assert over repository membership itself.
inputProfiles.emitted: Built package outputs, packed archive bytes, the native corpus and the host scripts an independent installed consumer executes.
inputProfiles.development-native-build: CLI source, canonical generator source, native owners and their captured teaching manifest.
inputProfiles.selected-tests: Owning production sources, every non-test helper, shared configuration and dependency sources; exclude only declared sibling test files, retaining selected and unassigned files.
inputProfiles.selected-tests-workspace-records: selected-tests plus authored workspace records, teaching resources and native fixture inventories read through the filesystem.
inputProfiles.language-conformance: workspace-records plus the compliance language fixtures read by the language formatter and conformance suites.
inputProfiles.host-adapters: workspace-records plus this repository's committed ia-authoring skills under .claude/skills and .agents/skills, the pending mandate-resolution note and consumed changeset history read by runtime tests through the filesystem, since no import edge names them.
inputProfiles.composition-fixture: workspace-records plus apps/cli's composition workspace fixture, whose authored records the workspace-runtime generator tests render through the filesystem, since no import edge names them.
inputProfiles.dependency-policy: Component package manifests and src trees scanned through filesystem discovery, including additions/removals, plus the dependency checker and execution inputs.
inputProfiles.test-configuration: Tooling plus each workspace project Vitest configuration read by inventory and temporary-directory policy tests.
inputProfiles.distribution-fixtures: Workspace records plus the distribution assets and fixtures used by distribution tests.
inputProfiles.qualification-source: The complete tracked source selection used by public package receipts, toolchain and source revision. Ordinary receipts and archives are verified during every consumer execution.

skips.reason: The case points ComSpec at node so that a started shell would print an unrecognizable message; only Windows would start that shell, so elsewhere the case cannot fail. Linux and macOS assert not-found through the relative and empty PATH entry cases.

skips.case: tests/host-plugin.test.ts > hook: the ia found runs through cmd.exe when ComSpec names node or spells cmd.exe with forward slashes (LKI-41)
skips.reason: Starts a real cmd.exe from SystemRoot under a ComSpec that only Windows reads; the emulated Windows cases check the same launch on Linux and macOS: the cmd.exe under SystemRoot whatever ComSpec names, /d /v:off /s /c and verbatim arguments.

skips.case: tests/host-plugin.test.ts > hook: a launcher on PATH that starts node by name cannot reach a node.cmd planted in the project (LKI-41)
skips.reason: cmd.exe's search of the current directory and NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath exist only on Windows; the POSIX launcher case covers a node behind a relative PATH entry on Linux and macOS.

skips.case: tests/host-plugin.test.ts > hook: doctor started from the recorded entry cannot reach a program in the project directory (LKI-41)
skips.reason: Only Windows' libuv searches the working directory first, and the plant is a copy of hostname.exe from System32; the POSIX doctor case covers a program behind a relative PATH entry on Linux and macOS.

skips.case: tests/host-plugin.test.ts > hook: an ia.exe starts directly, even under a path that cmd.exe would expand (crowncodes/ia#474)
skips.reason: Starts a real ia.exe, a link to or copy of this node.exe, from a directory whose name holds %OS%, which only cmd.exe would expand; the emulated Windows cases check on Linux and macOS that a .com or .exe starts directly and that only a .bat or .cmd path is passed over for a %.

skips.case: tests/host-plugin.test.ts > hook: with no qualified PATH entry doctor can still start a System32 program by name (crowncodes/ia#474)
skips.reason: Starts hostname.exe by name from the System32 directory under SystemRoot, which exists only on Windows; the platform-independent child PATH case checks the System32 fallback and the POSIX /usr/bin:/bin one on Linux and macOS.

skips.case: tests/host-plugin-node.test.ts > a node planted in the project or behind a relative PATH entry never starts the hook, and sh runs the recorded Node as written (crowncodes/ia#436)
skips.reason: On Windows the plugin hook keeps the earlier node command, which looks node up on PATH (host plugin distribution spec §6.1); the injected-platform Windows rendering case checks that command byte for byte on every platform.

skips.case: tests/host-plugin.test.ts > hook: a folder named ia and an ia without execute permission are passed over for the next PATH entry, as the shell would

skips.reason: A directory name can hold a quote on Linux and macOS but not on Windows, so the case cannot build its PATH there; the platform-independent child PATH case checks that Windows drops the quotes and POSIX keeps each entry as written.
